items.title: Introduction
items.text:
List Pocket is a self-hosted newsletter and mailing list manager. It keeps the core listmonk-style workflow (campaigns, lists, subscribers, APIs) while running entirely on embedded PocketBase — auth, collections, realtime, and the app’s SQL layer (SQLite under the hood). There is no separate PostgreSQL or other external database server.

The admin UI is a Vue 3 app; the server is a single Go binary.

items.title: Developers
items.text: List Pocket is free and open source software licensed under AGPLv3. See the GitHub repository and the developer setup. The backend is Go; the frontend is Vue with Vuetify.

items.title: AI and the agent
items.text: The Agent page, the assistant side panel, workflow AI steps and the campaign builder all use the provider chosen under Settings → AI.

items.title: Providers
items.text:
• API key. Set LISTPOCKET_AI_API_KEY, and optionally LISTPOCKET_AI_BASE_URL and LISTPOCKET_AI_MODEL. Any OpenAI-compatible service works. The assistant asks for replies of up to 128,000 tokens, or LISTPOCKET_AI_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS if you set it, where 0 asks for no limit. If a model refuses that, its own limit is used instead.
  • ChatGPT plan. Sign in with ChatGPT, and requests count toward your plan's Codex usage instead of per-token API costs. It needs Plus or Pro.

OpenAI offers plan usage for open-source and locally hosted apps. For a paid or remotely hosted deployment, they ask you to apply through their interest form.

items.title: Signing in
items.text:
Go to Settings → AI → Sign in with ChatGPT. List Pocket listens on 127.0.0.1:1455 for OpenAI's callback, so this finishes by itself when the browser and List Pocket are on the same computer. On a remote server, the sign-in ends on a page that can't be reached: copy that page's full address and paste it into the box on the settings page.

You can also import a session exported by Go-Harness (harness chatgpt login --export).

items.title: What's different on a plan
items.text:
• Run costs show as $0, so workflow AI budgets don't apply. Limit AI steps with their maximum steps setting instead.
  • Temperature and token limits aren't sent, because the plan route rejects them.
  • When the plan's limit is reached, requests fail until it resets. Switch model or provider to carry on.
  • Sessions renew automatically. Signing out revokes the session at OpenAI and returns anything defaulting to the plan to the API key.

Session tokens are stored in the oauth_credentials collection, which only superusers can read. They aren't encrypted separately from the rest of pb_data, so protect its backups accordingly.

items.title: The Agent page
items.text:
Conversations are private to the person who has them, and each can use its own model.

  • Context. Type @ or use Context to attach contacts, conversations, campaigns, lists, templates, workflows and runs. It's read fresh on each turn, through the same permissions as the rest of the app, so nobody can attach what they can't already see. Click anything attached to see what the agent sees.
  • Files. Attach or drop text files (up to 2 MB), images and PDFs (up to 6 MB), or paste data. Files go to the configured AI provider. Text files stay in context for the whole conversation, and images and PDFs are sent with the message they're attached to.
  • Proposals. The agent can read freely, but every change comes back as a proposal. Review opens a preview you can edit: a graph of what changes for workflows, the rendered email for campaigns and templates, and the exact text for replies. Nothing happens until you apply it. A proposal that fails isn't retried, because it may have partly worked.

items.title: Archives
items.text:
A global public archive is maintained on the public web interface. It can be enabled under Settings -> Settings -> General -> Enable public mailing list archive.

To make a campaign available in the public archive (provided it has been enabled in the settings as described above), enable the option 'Publish to public archive' under Campaigns -> Create new -> Archive.

When using template variables that depend on subscriber data (such as any template variable referencing .Subscriber), such data must be supplied as 'Campaign metadata', which is a JSON object that will be used in place of .Subscriber when rendering the archive template and content.

When individual subscriber tracking is enabled, TrackLink requires metadata for an existing subscriber (including the PocketBase record id in the id field). Any clicks on a TrackLink from the archived campaign will be counted towards that subscriber.

As an example:

{
  "id": "pbc_subscriber_record_id_here",
  "email": "example@example.com",
  "name": "Reader",
  "attribs": {}
}

items.title: Bounce processing
items.text: Enable bounce processing in Settings -> Bounces. POP3 bounce scanning and APIs only become available once the setting is enabled.

items.title: POP3 bounce mailbox
items.text:
Configure the bounce mailbox in Settings -> Bounces. Either the "From" e-mail that is set on a campaign (or in settings) should have a POP3 mailbox behind it to receive bounce e-mails, or you should configure a dedicated POP3 mailbox and add that address as the Return-Path (envelope sender) header in Settings -> SMTP -> Custom headers box. For example:

[
    {"Return-Path": "your-bounce-inbox@site.com"}
]

Some mail servers may also return the bounce to the Reply-To address, which can also be added to the header settings.

items.title: Bounce classification
items.text: List Pocket applies a series of heuristics looking for keywords in the bounced mail body to guess if it is a 'soft' bounce or a 'hard' bounce. For instance, 4.x.x and 5.x.x error status codes, common strings such as "mailbox not found" etc. If none of the heuristics match, then the bounce mail is considered to be 'soft' by default.

items.title: Webhook API
items.text:
The bounce webhook API can be used to record bounce events with custom scripting. This could be by reading a mailbox, a database, or mail server logs.

Method Endpoint Description POST /webhooks/bounce Record a bounce event. Name Type Required Description subscriber_uuid string The UUID of the subscriber. Either this or email is required. email string The e-mail of the subscriber. Either this or subscriber_uuid is required. campaign_uuid string UUID of the campaign for which the bounce happened. source string Yes A string indicating the source, eg: api, my_script etc. type string Yes hard or soft bounce. Currently, this has no effect on how the bounce is treated. meta string An optional escaped JSON string with arbitrary metadata about the bounce event. 
curl -u 'api_username:access_token' -X POST 'http://localhost:9000/webhooks/bounce' \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --data '{"email": "user1@mail.com", "campaign_uuid": "9f86b50d-5711-41c8-ab03-bc91c43d711b", "source": "api", "type": "hard", "meta": "{\"additional\": \"info\"}}'

items.title: External webhooks
items.text:
List Pocket supports receiving bounce webhook events from the following SMTP providers.

Endpoint Description More info https://listpocket.yoursite.com/webhooks/service/ses Amazon (AWS) SES See below https://listpocket.yoursite.com/webhooks/service/sendgrid Sendgrid / Twilio Signed event webhook More info https://listpocket.yoursite.com/webhooks/service/postmark Postmark webhook More info https://listpocket.yoursite.com/webhooks/service/forwardemail Forward Email webhook More info

items.title: Amazon Simple Email Service (SES)
items.text:
If using SES as your SMTP provider, automatic bounce processing is the recommended way to maintain your sender reputation. The settings below are based on Amazon's recommendations. Please note that your sending domain must be verified in SES before proceeding.

  1. In List Pocket settings, go to the "Bounces" tab and configure the following:
    • Enable bounce processing: Enabled
      • Soft:
        • Bounce count: 2
        • Action: None
      • Hard:
        • Bounce count: 1
        • Action: Blocklist
      • Complaint:
        • Bounce count: 1
        • Action: Blocklist
    • Enable bounce webhooks: Enabled
    • Enable SES: Enabled
  2. In the AWS console, go to Simple Notification Service and create a new topic with the following settings:
    • Type: Standard
    • Name: ses-bounces (or any other name)
  3. Create a new subscription to that topic with the following settings:
    • Protocol: HTTPS
    • Endpoint: https://listpocket.yoursite.com/webhooks/service/ses
    • Enable raw message delivery: Disabled (unchecked)
  4. SES will then make a request to your List Pocket instance to confirm the subscription. After a page refresh, the subscription should have a status of "Confirmed". If not, your endpoint may be incorrect or not publicly accessible.
  5. In the AWS console, go to Simple Email Service and click "Identities" in the left sidebar.
  6. Click your domain and go to the "Notifications" tab.
  7. Next to "Feedback notifications", click "Edit".
  8. For both "Bounce feedback" and "Complaint feedback", use the following settings:
    • SNS topic: ses-bounces (or whatever you named it)
    • Include original email headers: Enabled (checked)
  9. Repeat steps 6-8 for any Email address identities you send from using List Pocket
  10. Bounce processing should now be working. You can test it with SES simulator addresses. Add them as subscribers, send them campaign previews, and ensure that the appropriate action was taken after the configured bounce count was reached.
    • Soft bounce: ooto@simulator.amazonses.com
    • Hard bounce: bounce@simulator.amazonses.com
    • Complaint: complaint@simulator.amazonses.com
  11. You can optionally disable email feedback forwarding.

items.title: Exporting bounces
items.text:
Bounces can be exported via the JSON API: 

curl -u 'username:passsword' 'http://localhost:9000/api/bounces'

Or by querying the database directly: 

SELECT bounces.created_at,
    bounces.subscriber_id,
    subscribers.uuid AS subscriber_uuid,
    subscribers.email AS email
FROM bounces
LEFT JOIN subscribers ON (subscribers.id = bounces.subscriber_id)
ORDER BY bounces.created_at DESC LIMIT 1000;

items.title: Subscriber
items.text: A subscriber is a recipient identified by an e-mail address and name. Subscribers receive e-mails that are sent from List Pocket. A subscriber can be added to any number of lists. Subscribers who are not a part of any lists are considered orphan records.

items.title: Attributes
items.text:
Attributes are arbitrary properties attached to a subscriber in addition to their e-mail and name. They are represented as a JSON map. It is not necessary for all subscribers to have the same attributes. Subscribers can be queried and segmented into lists based on their attributes, and the attributes can be inserted into the e-mails sent to them. For example:

{
  "city": "Bengaluru",
  "likes_tea": true,
  "spoken_languages": ["English", "Malayalam"],
  "projects": 3,
  "stack": {
    "frameworks": ["echo", "go"],
    "languages": ["go", "python"],
    "preferred_language": "go"
  }
}

items.title: Subscription statuses
items.text:
A subscriber can be added to one or more lists, and each such relationship can have one of these statuses.

Status Description unconfirmed The subscriber was added to the list directly without their explicit confirmation. Nonetheless, the subscriber will receive campaign messages sent to single optin campaigns. confirmed The subscriber confirmed their subscription by clicking on 'accept' in the confirmation e-mail. Only confirmed subscribers in opt-in lists will receive campaign messages send to the list. unsubscribed The subscriber is unsubscribed from the list and will not receive any campaign messages sent to the list.

items.title: Segmentation
items.text: Segmentation is the process of filtering a large list of subscribers into a smaller group based on arbitrary conditions, primarily based on their attributes. For instance, if an e-mail needs to be sent subscribers who live in a particular city, given their city is described in their attributes, it's possible to quickly filter them out into a new list and e-mail them. Learn more.

items.title: List
items.text: A list (or a mailing list) is a collection of subscribers grouped under a name, for instance, clients. Lists are used to organise subscribers and send e-mails to specific groups. A list can be single optin or double optin. Subscribers added to double optin lists have to explicitly accept the subscription by clicking on the confirmation e-mail they receive. Until then, they do not receive campaign messages.

items.title: Campaign
items.text: A campaign is an e-mail (or any other kind of messages) that is sent to one or more lists.

items.title: Transactional message
items.text: A transactional message is an arbitrary message sent to a subscriber using the transactional message API. For example a welcome e-mail on signing up to a service; an order confirmation e-mail on purchasing an item; a password reset e-mail when a user initiates an online account recovery process.

items.title: Template
items.text: A template is a re-usable HTML design that can be used across campaigns and when sending arbitrary transactional messages. Most commonly, templates have standard header and footer areas with logos and branding elements, where campaign content is inserted in the middle. List Pocket supports Go template expressions that lets you create powerful, dynamic HTML templates. Learn more.

items.title: Messenger
items.text: List Pocket supports multiple custom messaging backends in additional to the default SMTP e-mail backend, enabling not just e-mail campaigns, but arbitrary message campaigns such as SMS, FCM notifications etc. A Messenger is a web service that accepts a campaign message pushed to it as a JSON request, which the service can in turn broadcast as SMS, FCM etc. Learn more.

items.title: Tracking pixel
items.text: The tracking pixel is a tiny, invisible image that is inserted into an e-mail body to track e-mail views. This allows measuring the read rate of e-mails. While this is exceedingly common in e-mail campaigns, it carries privacy implications and should be used in compliance with rules and regulations such as GDPR. It is possible to track reads anonymously without associating an e-mail read to a subscriber.

items.title: Click tracking
items.text: It is possible to track the clicks on every link that is sent in an e-mail. This allows measuring the clickthrough rates of links in e-mails. While this is exceedingly common in e-mail campaigns, it carries privacy implications and should be used in compliance with rules and regulations such as GDPR. It is possible to track link clicks anonymously without associating an e-mail read to a subscriber.

items.title: Bounce
items.text: A bounce occurs when an e-mail that is sent to a recipient "bounces" back for one of many reasons including the recipient address being invalid, their mailbox being full, or the recipient's e-mail service provider marking the e-mail as spam. List Pocket can automatically process such bounce e-mails that land in a configured POP mailbox, or via APIs of SMTP e-mail providers such as AWS SES and Sendgrid. Based on settings, subscribers returning bounced e-mails can either be blocklisted or deleted automatically. Learn more.

items.title: TOML Configuration file
items.text:
One or more TOML files can be read by passing --config config.toml multiple times. Apart from a few low-level options (such as [app] and built-in docs paths), all other settings can be managed from the Settings dashboard on the admin UI. There is no [db] block: persistence is entirely through embedded PocketBase (SQLite in pb_data/ by default).

To generate a new sample configuration file, run listpocket --new-config (or go run ./cmd -- --new-config during development).

items.title: Environment variables
items.text:
Variables in config.toml can also be provided as environment variables prefixed by LISTPOCKET_, with periods replaced by __ (double underscore). To start List Pocket using only environment variables, set the variables and pass --config="".

Example:

Environment variable Example value LISTPOCKET_app__address "0.0.0.0:9000" LISTPOCKET_app__docs_dir "/var/listpocket/docs" LISTPOCKET_app__swagger_dir "/var/listpocket/swagger"

PocketBase’s own flags (for example data directory) are passed through the PocketBase CLI embedded in the binary; see PocketBase configuration.

items.title: Built-in documentation URLs
items.text:
If docs/docs/_out (Zensical site_dir) and docs/swagger exist relative to the process working directory—or you set app.docs_dir / app.swagger_dir—the HTTP server exposes:

Path Content /docs/ Documentation manual (static HTML) /openapi.yaml OpenAPI 3 spec (collections.yaml) /swagger/ Swagger UI for the spec

items.text: See system templates.

items.title: Using filesystem
items.text:
When configuring docker volume mounts for using filesystem media uploads, you can follow either of two approaches. The second option may be necessary if your setup requires you to use sudo for docker commands.

After making any changes you will need to run sudo docker compose stop ; sudo docker compose up.

And under https://listpocket.mysite.com/admin/settings you put /listpocket/uploads (paths depend on your deployment).

items.title: Using volumes
items.text:
Using docker volumes, you can specify the name of volume and destination for the files to be uploaded inside the container.

app:
    volumes:
      - type: volume
        source: listpocket-uploads
        target: /listpocket/uploads

volumes:
  listpocket-uploads:

Note

This volume is managed by docker itself, and you can find the host path with docker volume inspect on your stack’s volume name.

items.title: Using bind mounts
items.text:
app:
    volumes:
      - ./path/on/your/host/:/path/inside/container
Eg: 
  app:
    volumes:
      - ./data/uploads:/listpocket/uploads
The files will be available inside /data/uploads directory on the host machine.

To use the default uploads folder: 

  app:
    volumes:
      - ./uploads:/listpocket/uploads

items.title: Docker
items.text:
https://docs.docker.com/engine/reference/commandline/logs/ 

sudo docker logs -f
sudo docker logs listpocket_app -t
sudo docker logs --help
Container info: sudo docker inspect on your compose project’s containers.

Docker logs to /dev/stdout and /dev/stderr. The logs are collected by the docker daemon and stored in your node's host path (by default). The same can be configured (/etc/docker/daemon.json) in your docker daemon settings to setup other logging drivers, logrotate policy and more, which you can read about here.

items.title: Binary
items.text:
List Pocket logs to stdout, which is usually not saved to any file. To save logs to a file you can redirect output, for example ./listpocket > listpocket.log.

Settings → Logs in the admin UI shows recent log lines from memory; they are cleared when the process restarts.

For a systemd unit, redirect ExecStart output to a file under /var/log or use journald — adapt the upstream listmonk service example for the listpocket binary and your paths.

items.title: Time zone
items.text:
To change the process time zone (logs, etc.) when using Docker Compose, edit docker-compose.yml: 

environment:
    - TZ=Etc/UTC
with any Timezone listed here. Then run sudo docker-compose stop ; sudo docker-compose up after making changes.

items.title: Retries
items.text: The Settings -> SMTP -> Retries denotes the number of times a message that fails at the moment of sending is retried silently using different connections from the SMTP pool. The messages that fail even after retries are the ones that are logged as errors and ignored.

items.title: SMTP ports
items.text: Some server hosts block outgoing SMTP ports (25, 465). You may have to contact your host to unblock them before being able to send e-mails. Eg: Hetzner.

items.title: Batch size
items.text: The batch size parameter is useful when working with very large lists with millions of subscribers for maximising throughput. It is the number of subscribers that are fetched from the database sequentially in a single cycle (~5 seconds) when a campaign is running. Increasing the batch size uses more memory, but reduces the round trip to the database.

items.title: Developer setup
items.text: The app has two parts: the Go backend (with embedded PocketBase) and the Vue 3 frontend. In development they run as separate processes.

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
• Go (see go.mod for the toolchain version)
  • Node.js and npm (for the frontend)

items.title: First-time setup
items.text:
1. Clone this repository (it uses Go modules; clone outside GOPATH/src if you still use legacy layouts).
  2. Copy config.toml.sample to config.toml and set [app] as needed.
  3. From the repo root, build the frontend and run the backend (see below).

MailHog is a useful mock SMTP server with a web UI for local e-mail testing.

items.title: Running locally
items.text:
1. Backend — from the repository root:
go run ./cmd

By default the app listens on http://127.0.0.1:9000. PocketBase stores its data under pb_data/ (SQLite) in the working directory unless you change PocketBase’s data dir.

  1. Frontend — in a second terminal:
cd frontend
npm install
npm run dev

The dev server (default http://127.0.0.1:8080) proxies /api/* to the backend.

See the frontend README for structure and conventions.

items.title: Production build
items.text:
Build the frontend, then compile the binary:

cd frontend && npm install && npm run build
cd .. && go build -o listpocket ./cmd

This embeds static templates, i18n packs, permissions, and the sample config into the binary. Serve the admin UI from frontend/dist on disk (built in the previous step). Run ./listpocket with your config.toml (and optional LISTPOCKET_* environment variables).

items.title: Integrating with external systems
items.text: In many environments, a mailing list manager's subscriber database is not run independently but as a part of an existing customer database or a CRM. There are multiple ways of keeping List Pocket in sync with external systems.

items.title: Using APIs
items.text: The subscriber APIs offers several APIs to manipulate the subscribers database, like addition, updation, and deletion. For bulk synchronisation, a CSV can be generated (and optionally zipped) and posted to the import API.

items.title: Interacting directly with the DB
items.text: listpocket stores subscribers, lists, and subscriptions in PocketBase collections. For advanced integrations in this fork, use the app APIs and PocketBase collection definitions rather than the old SQL schema from upstream listmonk.

items.title: Internationalization (i18n)
items.text: List Pocket ships with multiple languages via JSON language packs (the same general model as upstream listmonk). Bundled files live in the repository under i18n/.

items.title: Additional language packs
items.text:
Community packs written for listmonk often work as-is because the key structure is inherited. Download any extra .json files and pass their directory to the binary with --i18n-dir=/path/to/dir.

Language Description Deutsch (formal) Example third-party pack (upstream listmonk)

items.title: Customizing languages
items.text: Put one or more .json language files in a directory and start the app with --i18n-dir=/path/to/dir.

items.title: Using the basic editor
items.text:
The repository includes a small static editor under docs/i18n/ (open index.html in a browser or serve the folder locally).

  • Translate the strings in the UI.
  • Use Download raw JSON to export the file.
  • Open a pull request adding the file to the i18n/ directory in this repository.

items.title: Upstream Inlang (optional)
items.text: The listmonk Inlang project tracks translations for stock listmonk. You can use it as a reference; contributions to List Pocket should target this repository’s i18n folder.

items.title: Installation
items.text: List Pocket ships as source in this repository. It is a Go application built around embedded PocketBase for all persistence, authentication, and realtime features. Data is stored in PocketBase’s SQLite database (by default under pb_data/). There is no published Docker image or third-party one-click installer for this fork; deploy by building the binary yourself or wrapping it in your own container.

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
• Go (see go.mod for the toolchain)
  • Node.js/npm (to build the admin frontend from source)

items.title: Build and run
items.text:
1. Clone the repository: git clone https://github.com/compdani/list_pocket.git
  2. Copy config.toml.sample to config.toml and adjust [app] (e.g. address) as needed.
  3. Build the frontend and backend (see the repository README or Developer setup).
  4. Run the listpocket binary and open the app (default http://127.0.0.1:9000).

Environment variables override config.toml when prefixed with LISTPOCKET_; see Configuration.

items.title: Database and migrations
items.text: All application data goes through PocketBase. Schema migrations run on serve/startup (PocketBase bootstrap). You can also run listpocket migrate up. The --install and --upgrade CLI flags are deprecated no-ops kept for older listmonk-style automation.

items.title: Relationship to listmonk
items.text: List Pocket inherits concepts and APIs from listmonk. Upstream guides that assume a standalone PostgreSQL server and LISTMONK_* / [db] settings describe stock listmonk, not this project’s PocketBase-only stack.

items.title: Messengers
items.text:
List Pocket supports multiple custom messaging backends in additional to the default SMTP e-mail backend, enabling not just e-mail campaigns, but arbitrary message campaigns such as SMS, FCM notifications etc.

A Messenger is a web service that accepts a campaign message pushed to it as a JSON request, which the service can in turn broadcast as SMS, FCM etc. Messengers are registered in the Settings -> Messengers UI, and can be selected on individual campaigns.

Messengers support optional BasicAuth authentication. Plain text format for campaign content is ideal for messengers such as SMS and FCM.

When a campaign starts, List Pocket POSTs messages in the following format to the selected messenger's endpoint. The endpoint should return a 200 OK response in case of a successful request.

The address required to broadcast the message, for instance, a phone number or an FCM ID, is expected to be stored and relayed as subscriber attributes. 

{
    "subject": "Welcome to List Pocket",
    "body": "The message body",
    "content_type": "plain",
    "recipients": [{
        "uuid": "e44b4135-1e1d-40c5-8a30-0f9a886c2884",
        "email": "anon@example.com",
        "name": "Anon Doe",
        "attribs": {
            "phone": "123123123",
            "fcm_id": "2e7e4b512e7e4b512e7e4b51",
            "city": "Bengaluru"
        },
        "status": "enabled"
    }],
    "campaign": {
        "uuid": "2e7e4b51-f31b-418a-a120-e41800cb689f",
        "name": "Test campaign",
        "tags": ["test-campaign"]
    }
}

items.title: Messenger implementations
items.text:
Following is a list of HTTP messenger servers that connect to various backends.

Name Backend listmonk-messenger AWS Pinpoint SMS (listmonk-compatible webhook) listmonk-verimor-gateway Verimor listmonk-mailersend Mailersend listmonk-novu-messenger Novu listmonk-push-messenger Google FCM

These community projects target upstream listmonk’s messenger protocol; List Pocket keeps the same JSON payload shape where possible.

items.title: WhatsApp
items.text: WhatsApp is built in, and doesn't use a postback messenger. See WhatsApp.

items.title: OIDC Single Sign On
items.text: List Pocket supports single sign-on with OIDC (OpenID Connect). Any standards compliant OIDC provider can be configured in Settings -> Security -> OIDC

items.title: User auto-creation
items.text: If Settings -> Security -> OIDC -> Auto-create users is turned on, when users login via OIDC, an account is auto-created if an existing account is not found (based on the OIDC e-mail ID).

items.title: Tutorials
items.text: Tutorials for configuring List Pocket SSO with popular OIDC providers.

items.title: Keycloak
items.text: Keycloak configuration for List Pocket SSO integration.

items.title: 1. Create a new client in Keycloak
items.text:
In the Keycloak admin, use an existing realm, or create a new realm. Create a new client in Clients → Create.

  • General Settings
    • Client type: OpenID Connect
    • Client ID: listpocket (or any preferred name)
    • Name: Optional descriptive name (e.g., "List Pocket SSO")
  • Capability Config:
    • Client authentication: On
    • Authorization: On
    • Authentication Flow
      • Standard Flow: On
      • Direct Access grants: On
  • Login Settings:
    • Root URL: Copy the Redirect URL for oAuth provider value from List Pocket Admin -> Settings -> Security -> OIDC. It will look like https://listpocket.yoursite.com/auth/oidc
    • Valid redirect URIs: Same as the Root URL above
    • Valid post logout redirect URIs: *

After the client creation steps above, go to the client's Credentials tab and copy the Client Secret.

items.title: 2. Configure List Pocket
items.text:
1. In List Pocket Admin -> Settings -> Security -> OIDC.
    • Enable OIDC SSO: Turn on
    • Provider URL: https://keycloak.yoursite.com/realms/{realm} (replace {realm} with the chosen realm name). This URL is as of v26.3 and may differ across Keycloak versions.
    • Provider name: Set a name to show on the List Pocket login form, eg: Login with OrgName

    • Client Secret: Client Secret copied from Keycloak
    • Auto-create users from SSO: (Optional) Enable to automatically create users who don't exist
