items.title: Plugins
items.text:
A plugin adds to a running List Pocket without a rebuild. It can:

  • send new types of message, including new channels with their own addresses and consent
  • receive webhooks at its own URLs
  • add pages, settings tabs and other UI to the admin
  • add tools, events, agent presets and field editors to workflows

Only super admins can install plugins. A plugin runs with full access to the app and its data, so only install plugins you trust. Its browser code can act as any logged-in admin who loads it.

examples/plugins/telegram is a complete working plugin that uses all of this.

items.title: Add-on types
items.text:
A plugin declares what it adds in its manifest, and can add any mix of these. The Plugins page lists what each one adds.

Add-on Manifest key Code What it adds Channel channels plugin.channel A new way to send campaigns and messages Webhook webhooks plugin.webhook A public URL that receives requests Admin route adminRoutes plugin.adminRoute An API for the plugin's own UI Settings settings None A generated tab under Settings Admin UI ui host.routes, host.nav, host.slots Pages, navigation and page sections Workflow tool tools plugin.tool An action for Tool nodes and agents Workflow event events host.workflows.emit Something a workflow can start on or wait for Agent preset agentPresets None A ready-made agent for Agent nodes Field editor fieldEditors host.fields.add A custom input for a tool's field

Plugins add to workflows through tools rather than new node types. A tool already works with approvals, agents, retries and run history.

items.title: Building a plugin with the assistant
items.text:
Super admins can ask the AI assistant to write or change a plugin, from the assistant panel or the Agent page. Build with AI on the Plugins page opens it. Other roles don't have these tools.

The assistant can read this guide and an installed plugin's source. It works in a draft, which it can write a few files at a time and change with targeted edits. A draft of an installed plugin starts as a copy of it. Drafts are saved on the server, so they outlast a conversation turn and a restart. They run nothing and aren't installed, so writing to one needs no approval. An untouched draft is removed after 30 days. Stored settings and secrets aren't available to the assistant.

When the draft is finished, the assistant proposes it:

  1. Its manifest and script syntax are checked, and the assistant fixes any errors it gets back. None of the plugin's code runs at this point, so a plugin that passes may still fail to load.
  2. Open Review to read the code. You can edit it there. For a new version, you can also see what changed from the installed one.
  3. Install adds it, disabled, and removes the draft. A new version of an installed plugin keeps its images and other files that aren't text.
  4. Enable it under Settings → Plugins. The app restarts, and any load error appears on that page. Ask the assistant to read it and fix the problem.

Installing a new version of an enabled plugin needs no further approval to go live: it takes over at the next restart, even one you didn't start for this reason. Disable the plugin first if you aren't ready for that.

Only plain text files can be written this way: .js, .mjs, .json, .css, .md, .txt, .svg and .html, up to 2 MiB of source in all. Upload a zip for anything else. A draft of a plugin that's already been replaced by an upload can't be proposed, because it would undo that upload. The assistant has to start it again.

Inbound messages and other data can try to steer an AI model. Be wary of any plugin you didn't ask for, whatever it says it's for.

items.title: Installing
items.text:
Go to Settings → Plugins → Install plugin and upload a zip. A new plugin stays disabled until you enable it.

Action Takes effect Install, change settings Straight away Enable, disable, upgrade, uninstall After an automatic restart, which waits for running campaigns

A plugin can't be disabled while a running or scheduled campaign uses one of its channels.

You can also copy a plugin to <pb_data>/plugins/<id>/<version>/. It's found at the next start and stays disabled until you enable it.

items.title: If a plugin stops the app from starting
items.text:
Set LISTPOCKET_plugins__safe_mode=true to start with no plugins loaded, then disable or uninstall the plugin. A plugin that only fails to load doesn't need this: it's marked as failed and the app carries on. If a campaign's channel is unavailable, the campaign pauses rather than being cancelled.

To test the admin UI without any plugin's browser code, add ?plugins=off to the URL.

items.title: Package layout
items.text:
plugin.json     the manifest
server.js       server-side code
ui/index.js     optional browser module; only ui/ is served publicly
i18n/en.json    optional messages

items.title: Manifest
items.text:
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "id": "telegram",
  "name": "Telegram",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "server": { "entry": "server.js", "concurrency": 4, "timeoutMs": 15000 },
  "ui": { "entry": "ui/index.js", "css": ["ui/index.css"] },
  "channels": [{
    "id": "ch:telegram",
    "label": "Telegram",
    "icon": "<SVG path data>",
    "addressSource": "channel",
    "addressLabel": "Chat ID",
    "contentTypes": ["plain"],
    "campaignFields": [{ "key": "disable_preview", "type": "boolean", "label": "Hide link previews" }],
    "rateLimit": { "maxPerSecond": 25 }
  }],
  "webhooks": [{ "path": "inbound", "methods": ["POST"], "maxBodyBytes": 1048576 }],
  "adminRoutes": [{ "path": "contacts", "methods": ["GET"], "permission": "plugin_telegram:manage" }],
  "settings": [{ "key": "bot_token", "type": "secret", "label": "Bot token", "required": true }],
  "permissions": [{ "group": "plugin_telegram", "permissions": ["plugin_telegram:manage"] }],
  "i18n": { "en": "i18n/en.json" }
}
  • id: lowercase letters, numbers and underscores, starting with a letter. whatsapp is reserved for the built-in channel.
  • Channel IDs: ch:<plugin id> or ch:<plugin id>_<name>.
  • addressSource: channel keeps addresses in their own table. phone uses the subscriber's phone number.
  • contentTypes: only plain is supported.
  • campaignBody: set to none to hide the campaign's content step, for channels that send something else, such as a provider-side template. A UI slot can set the channel's options on campaign.channelFields.
  • settings and campaignFields types: text, textarea, secret, select (with options), number or boolean. Settings get a generated tab under Settings, so a plugin needs no UI code for configuration.
  • Permission groups: must be plugin_<id>. To label a group on the role form, add globals.terms.plugin_<id> to your messages.

items.title: Server code
items.text:
server.js is a classic script, with no import. It runs on a small pool of JavaScript VMs that share nothing, so keep state in host.kv, not in globals. Host calls are synchronous and there's no setTimeout. A call that runs past timeoutMs is stopped.

plugin.channel('ch:telegram', {
  send(msg) {
    // msg.to, msg.body, msg.subscriber, msg.campaign
    // msg.fields: your campaignFields, or the data of a transactional message
    return { providerMsgId: '123', invalidAddresses: [] };
  },
});

plugin.webhook('inbound', {
  verify(req) { return req.verifyHmacSha256(host.settings.get().secret, req.headers['x-signature'], { prefix: 'sha256=' }); },
  handle(req) { return { status: 200, json: { ok: true } }; },
});

plugin.adminRoute('contacts', (req) => ({ json: { contacts: [] } }));

items.title: Sending
items.text: Throw host.errors.unsendable('reason') if the recipient can never receive this, or return their addresses in invalidAddresses. Those addresses are retired and the recipient isn't retried. Any other error counts as a retryable send failure, and too many pause the campaign.

items.title: Webhooks
items.text:
Webhooks are public, at /webhooks/plugins/<id>/<path>. verify is required unless the manifest says "verify": "none", and it must return exactly true.

Response Meaning 404 Unknown or disabled plugin, or unknown path 405, 413 Method not declared, or body over maxBodyBytes 401 verify didn't return true 503, 504 All VMs busy, or the handler timed out 500 The handler threw. Details go to the log only

req has method, path, query, headers (lowercase), body, bodyBase64, json(), verifyHmacSha256(secret, signature, { prefix, encoding }) and once(key, ttlSeconds). A handler that returns nothing sends 200 {"ok":true}; otherwise return { status, headers, json } or { status, headers, body }.

Always use verifyHmacSha256 for body signatures. It checks the raw bytes in constant time, and a string in JavaScript can't round-trip them. Providers retry, so use req.once to handle each delivery once.

items.title: Host API
items.text:
Call Purpose host.settings.get() Stored settings, including secrets host.kv.get(key), set(key, value, { ttlSeconds }), delete(key) Plugin storage host.fetch(url, { method, headers, body, timeoutMs }) HTTP. Returns status, ok, headers, body, bodyBase64, json() host.log.info(...), warn, error Logging. Secret setting values are redacted host.crypto.hmacSha256Hex, sha256Hex, timingSafeEqual Crypto helpers host.contacts.findByAddress(channel, address), get(id) Look up a contact, or null host.contacts.upsertByAddress(channel, address, { name, lists, consent, source }) Find or create a contact. lists takes list UUIDs, and source records where consent came from host.contacts.setConsent(id, listId, channel, status, { source }) confirmed or unsubscribed host.contacts.importSMSConsent(channel, { dryRun, includeInherited }) Grant consent from SMS consent. Returns explicit, inherited and applied counts. Existing consent rows are never overwritten host.events.record({ channel, direction, kind, status, providerMsgId, subscriberId, address, body, payload }) Add to the subscriber's timeline. Returns false for a repeated providerMsgId host.events.status(channel, providerMsgId, status, { permanent }) Delivery update for a sent message. permanent also records a hard bounce and retires the address host.events.list({ subscriberId, channel, limit }) A subscriber's latest events, newest first host.events.counts(campaignId) A campaign's sends by delivery status host.events.bounce({ channel, subscriberId, campaignId, type, meta }) Record a bounce. Email bounce actions don't run for it host.events.optOut(channel, address) Withdraw consent on that channel, for everyone who owns the address host.messages.send({ channel, subscriberId, subject, body }) Send one message, if the contact has consented host.workflows.emit(event, payload) Raise one of this plugin's workflow events

A plugin can only use its own channels.

items.title: Workflow add-ons
items.text: Workflow add-ons are named <plugin id>.<name> everywhere they're used. Names use lowercase letters, numbers and underscores. If a workflow's plugin is disabled, publishing it fails validation and any run that reaches the missing tool or preset fails with an error saying so.

items.title: Workflow tools
items.text:
A tool appears in the builder's Tool node and in an Agent node's tool list. The assistant can also find it when it builds workflows.

"tools": [{
  "name": "get_chat",
  "description": "Look up a Telegram chat by ID.",
  "readOnly": true,
  "inputSchema": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": { "chat_id": { "type": "string", "description": "Telegram chat ID" } },
    "required": ["chat_id"]
  }
}]

plugin.tool('get_chat', (input, ctx) => {
  // ctx.config is this workflow's tool_config for the tool. ctx.runId is the workflow
  // run's ID in a Tool node, or the agent run's ID when an agent calls it.
  return { title: 'General' };
});
  • description: required. Models read it to decide when to use the tool, so say what it does and when to use it.
  • inputSchema: input is checked against it before your handler runs.
  • outputSchema: optional. It says what the tool returns, so the workflow builder can suggest its fields in JavaScript steps and models know what to read. It isn't checked against what your handler returns.
  • readOnly: set this only if the tool changes and sends nothing.
  • requiresApproval: a person approves each call from a Tool node. It defaults to true unless the tool is read-only. Agents can't pause for approval, so an agent that calls a tool needing it gets an error back. Setting it to false on a tool with side effects lets workflows and agents act with no check, so only do that for low-risk actions.
  • Results: return any JSON value, up to 1 MiB. Later nodes read it as nodes.<id>, and models see it, so never return a secret.
  • Errors: throw to fail the call. Secret setting values are removed from the message. A model can read the error and try again.

The name of the plugin and the tool can be 62 characters together. A tool can't replace one that already exists: it's skipped and the log says why.

items.title: Workflow events
items.text:
"events": [{ "name": "message_received", "description": "Someone messaged the bot. event: {chat_id, text}" }]

host.workflows.emit('message_received', { chat_id: '42', text: 'Hello' });

Workflows can then start on telegram.message_received or wait for it, and read the payload as event.*. Say what the payload holds in the description, because that's what people and models see when they pick the event. Payloads can be up to 1 MiB.

Only emit from a handler, not while the script loads. Emit once for each real event: webhook providers retry, so check req.once first. Anyone who can reach an unverified webhook can trigger what it emits, so verify the request before you emit.

items.title: Agent presets
items.text:
A preset is a ready-made agent. No code is needed.

"agentPresets": [{
  "name": "reply_drafter",
  "description": "Drafts a short reply.",
  "systemPrompt": "Draft a reply to: {{ .input.text }}",
  "tools": ["telegram.get_chat"],
  "maxSteps": 3,
  "outputSchema": { "type": "object", "properties": { "reply": { "type": "string" } } }
}]

Only name and systemPrompt are required. ai sets model options. Anything set on the Agent node overrides the preset, and the node's tools replace the preset's rather than adding to them. Workflows warn about tools with side effects in a preset the same way they do for the node's own tools.

items.title: Field editors
items.text:
A field editor replaces the plain input for one field of a tool in the builder.

"fieldEditors": [{ "name": "chat", "description": "Pick a chat." }],
"tools": [{ "name": "get_chat", "description": "…", "inputSchema": { "type": "object", "properties": {
  "chat_id": { "type": "string", "x-ui": "telegram.chat" }
} } }]

export default function setup(host) {
  host.fields.add('chat', defineComponent({
    props: ['modelValue', 'label', 'hint', 'readonly', 'schema', 'options'],
    emits: ['update:modelValue'],
    setup(props, { emit }) { /* render an input */ },
  }));
}

x-ui is an editor's name, or { "widget": "telegram.chat", ...options } to pass options to it. An editor needs a ui entry, and it can be used by another plugin's tools. If it isn't running, the field gets a plain input, so the stored value must make sense on its own. People can also type {{ }} expressions into tool inputs, so an editor shouldn't reject them.

items.title: Consent
items.text:
Channel consent is separate from email and SMS. A contact gets a campaign on a plugin channel only if they have confirmed consent for one of its lists on that channel and an active address. With no consent row, nothing is sent. Opt-in campaigns aren't available on plugin channels.

An opt-out is channel-wide and stays until new consent is given. A rejected address is different: it stops sends to that address but isn't an opt-out, and a message from that address clears it. Status updates can arrive in any order, including before the send is recorded, and never move backwards.

A contact created by upsertByAddress has no email. They're stored with a placeholder under no-email.invalid, which is never shown or sent to and can't be claimed by anyone. Entering a real address on their subscriber page replaces it.

items.title: Browser code
items.text:
ui/index.js is an ES module that exports a setup function. Imports of vue, vuetify and vuetify/components resolve to the host's copies, so keep them external if you use a bundler. Global Vuetify components such as v-btn are available through resolveComponent.

import { defineComponent, h, resolveComponent } from 'vue';

export default function setup(host) {
  const Page = defineComponent({
    setup: () => () => h(resolveComponent('v-alert'), { text: host.t('telegram.note') }),
  });

  host.routes.add({ name: 'contacts', path: 'contacts', title: 'telegram.contacts', component: Page, permission: 'plugin_telegram:manage' });
  host.nav.add({ route: 'contacts', label: 'Contacts', icon: '<SVG path data>', parent: 'settings' });
  host.settings.addTab({ key: 'advanced', label: 'Advanced', component: Page });
  host.slots.add('subscriber.form.after', Page);
}
  • host also has fetch(path, options) for your adminRoutes, fields for field editors, t, can, router and toast.
  • Paths and names are namespaced: the route above is /plugins/telegram/contacts.
  • Icons: use SVG path data. Named mdi-* icons only work if the host already bundles them.
  • Slots: campaign.form.after, template.form.after, subscriber.form.after, subscriber.activity.item, dashboard.widgets.
  • Failures: a module that throws or takes over 5 seconds is reported on the Plugins page and skipped. A component that throws is replaced by an error notice.
  • Secrets: files in ui/ are served without login, so never put secrets in them.

items.title: Querying and segmenting subscribers
items.text:
List Pocket supports two ways to segment subscribers:

  1. Visual filters (recommended) — build conditions on tags, attributes, status, email/name/phone, and list membership without writing SQL.
  2. SQL expressions — partial SQLite WHERE fragments for power users (requires the subscribers:sql_query permission).

items.title: Visual filters
items.text:
On the Subscribers page, open Filters and add conditions. Conditions in the main group are combined with AND. Use Add OR group when any of several conditions should match.

Supported fields:

Field Examples Tag Has any / all / none of selected tags (attribs.tags) Attribute Equals, contains, exists, numeric comparisons on JSON keys (including dotted paths like stack.preferred_language) Email / name / phone Equals, contains, starts with, ends with Status Is / is not enabled, disabled, or blocklisted List In / not in selected lists

Filters are sent to the API as a structured filters JSON payload and compiled server-side into parameterized SQL. They do not require the SQL permission.

items.title: Example filters payload
items.text:
{
  "logic": "and",
  "rules": [
    { "field": "tag", "op": "has_any", "value": ["vip"] },
    { "field": "attrib", "key": "city", "op": "eq", "value": "Bengaluru" },
    {
      "logic": "or",
      "rules": [
        { "field": "email", "op": "contains", "value": "@acme.com" },
        { "field": "attrib", "key": "company", "op": "eq", "value": "Acme" }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

items.title: Database fields (SQL)
items.text:
These are the fields in the subscriber database that can be queried with raw SQL.

Field Description subscribers.uuid The randomly generated unique ID of the subscriber subscribers.email E-mail ID of the subscriber subscribers.name Name of the subscriber subscribers.status Status of the subscriber (enabled, disabled, blocklisted) subscribers.attribs Map of arbitrary attributes represented as JSON (use SQLite JSON1 functions). subscribers.created Timestamp when the subscriber was first added (exposed as created_at in the API) subscribers.updated Timestamp when the subscriber was modified (exposed as updated_at in the API)

items.title: Sample attributes
items.text:
Here's a sample JSON map of attributes assigned to an imaginary subscriber.

{
  "city": "Bengaluru",
  "likes_tea": true,
  "spoken_languages": ["English", "Malayalam"],
  "projects": 3,
  "tags": ["vip", "demo-booked"],
  "stack": {
    "frameworks": ["echo", "go"],
    "languages": ["go", "python"],
    "preferred_language": "go"
  }
}

items.title: Sample SQL query expressions
items.text: Raw SQL is available under Filters → SQL for users with the subscribers:sql_query permission.

items.title: Find a subscriber by e-mail
items.text:
-- Exact match
subscribers.email = 'some@domain.com'

-- Partial match to find e-mails that end in @domain.com.
subscribers.email LIKE '%@domain.com'

items.title: Find a subscriber by name
items.text:
-- Find all subscribers whose name start with John.
subscribers.name LIKE 'John%'

items.title: Multiple conditions
items.text:
-- Find all Johns who have been blocklisted.
subscribers.name LIKE 'John%' AND subscribers.status = 'blocklisted'

items.title: Querying subscribers who viewed the campaign email
items.text:
-- Find all subscribers who viewed the campaign email.
EXISTS(
  SELECT 1 FROM campaign_views
  WHERE campaign_views.subscriber_id = subscribers.id
    AND campaign_views.campaign_id = <put_id_of_campaign>
)

items.title: Querying attributes (SQLite JSON1)
items.text:
-- Find subscribers in Bengaluru with more than 3 projects.
json_extract(subscribers.attribs, '$.city') = 'Bengaluru'
  AND CAST(json_extract(subscribers.attribs, '$.projects') AS REAL) > 3

items.title: Querying nested attributes
items.text:
subscribers.status = 'blocklisted'
  AND json_extract(subscribers.attribs, '$.likes_tea') = 1
  AND EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM json_each(json_extract(subscribers.attribs, '$.stack.languages'))
    WHERE value = 'python'
  )
  AND json_extract(subscribers.attribs, '$.stack.preferred_language') = 'go'

items.title: Querying tags
items.text:
-- Has any of these tags:
EXISTS (
  SELECT 1
  FROM json_each(COALESCE(json_extract(subscribers.attribs, '$.tags'), '[]')) jt
  WHERE lower(trim(CAST(jt.value AS TEXT))) IN ('vip', 'demo-booked')
)

To learn more about JSON expressions, see SQLite’s JSON1 extension (PocketBase uses SQLite under the hood).

items.title: User roles and permissions
items.text: List Pocket supports creating system users with granular permissions to various features, including list-specific permissions. Users can log in with a username and password, or via an OIDC (OpenID Connect) handshake if an auth provider is connected. Various permissions can be grouped into "user roles", which can be assigned to users. List-specific permissions can be grouped into "list roles".

items.title: User roles
items.text:
A user role is a collection of user related permissions. User roles are attached to user accounts. User roles can be managed in Admin -> Users -> User roles The permissions are described below.

Group Permission Description lists lists:get_all Get details of all lists lists:manage_all Create, update, and delete all lists subscribers subscribers:get Get individual subscriber details subscribers:get_all Get all subscribers and their details subscribers:manage Add, update, and delete subscribers subscribers:import Import subscribers from external files subscribers:sql_query Run raw SQL queries on subscriber data.WARNING:This permission allows execution of arbitrary SQL expressions and SQL functions. While it is readonly on the table data, it allows querying of all lists and subscribers directly from the database superceding individual list and subscriber permissions. Raw SQL can expose schema and engine details. Give this permission ONLY to trusted users. Learn more. tx:send Send transactional messages to subscribers campaigns campaigns:get Get and view campaigns belonging to permitted lists campaigns:get_all Get and view campaigns across all lists campaigns:get_analytics Access campaign performance metrics campaigns:manage Create, update, and delete campaigns bounces bounces:get Get email bounce records bounces:manage Process and handle bounced emails webhooks:post_bounce Receive bounce notifications via webhook media media:get Get uploaded media files media:manage Upload, update, and delete media templates templates:get Get email templates templates:manage Create, update, and delete templates users users:get Get system user accounts users:manage Create, update, and delete user accounts WARNING:This permission allows creation of users with any role, including Super Admin. This permission should only be given to Super Admin level accounts roles:get Get user roles and permissions roles:manage Create and modify user roles settings settings:get Get system settings settings:manage Modify system configuration settings:maintain Perform system maintenance tasks

items.title: List roles
items.text: A list role is a collection of permissions assigned per list. Each list can be assigned a view (read) or manage (update) permission. List roles are attached to user accounts. Only the lists defined in a list role is accessible by the user, be it on the admin UI or via API calls. Do note that the lists:get_all and lists:manage_all permissions in user roles override all per-list permissions.

items.title: API users
items.text: A user account can be of two types, a regular user or an API user. API users are meant for interacting with the HTTP APIs programmatically. Unlike regular user accounts that have custom passwords or OIDC for authentication, API users get an automatically generated secret token.

items.title: subscribers:sql_query
items.text:
This permission allowers users to write and execute arbitrary SQL queries on the database. Although it is executed as a read-only transaction disallowing changing of data in the database tables, it allows querying of all lists, subscribers and other data directly from the database superceding individual list and subscriber permissions.

Raw SQL expressions can expose database engine and schema details. Give this permission ONLY to trusted users.

List Pocket runs on PocketBase’s embedded SQLite database; there is no separate PostgreSQL role layer. Limit this permission to accounts that truly need ad hoc reporting over subscriber data.

items.title: Security reports
items.text: If you spot a security vulnerability in List Pocket, please report it via GitHub security advisories on this repository.

items.title: Subscriber SQL queries
items.text:
The subscribers UI (and APIs) support issuing of arbitrary SQL expressions via a query parameter. While List Pocket ensures that the queries are executed as readonly and has basic checks for target tables to prevent accidental side-effects, it is not really possible to prevent arbitrary Turing-complete SQL expressions from calling various SQLite built-in functions. SQLite does not offer a fine-grained way to allow or disallow specific functions per connection in this context.

That's why this feature is behind a special permission subscribers:sql_query and its risks are documented in User roles and permissions. In a multi-user scenario, it is up to an admin to allow this permission to trusted users.

items.title: Media uploads
items.text: In addition to images, List Pocket allows uploading of arbitrary file types, .html, .js, .svg, .* and does not transform or modify the files. That means, it is possible to have <script>s and other arbitrary content inside HTML and SVG files. It is not possible for the app to have special checks or transformations for various file types, and many environments legitimately want SVGs and other filetypes to be uploaded.

items.title: Campaign HTML
items.text: List Pocket is a full-fledged HTML content management system (similar to WordPress). It allows campaign messages to have arbitrary HTML, including <script>s, which is a legitimate use case in many environments. While campaign previews within the admin are iframe-sandboxed, when a campaign is published as a webpage (archive view), it will obviously execute whatever <script> it has. This is expected of a content management and publishing system. In a multi-user scenario, it is up to the admin to give appropriate permissions to trusted users if they deem this undesirable.

items.title: Templates
items.text: List Pocket is a full-fledged HTML content management system (similar to WordPress) which provides the full power of the Go templating language in addition to bundling Sprig functions. This allows executing Turing-complete code within templates where it is possible to write code that does loop-within-loop or memory-allocation code that runs within loops that could cause a DoS. There is no way to prevent this. In a multi-user scenario, it is up to the admin to give appropriate permissions to trusted users if they deem this undesirable.

items.title: Templating
items.text:
A template is a re-usable HTML design that can be used across campaigns and transactional messages. Most commonly, templates have standard header and footer areas with logos and branding elements, where campaign content is inserted in the middle.

List Pocket supports Go template expressions that lets you create powerful, dynamic HTML templates. It also integrates 100+ useful Sprig template functions.

Warning

Sprig template functions are powerful and Turing-complete, allowing programming of complex behaviour in templates. This means that it is also possible to program undesired behaviour, such as overloading memory on the host by concatenating large strings in a loop. Ensure that templating (campaigns, templates) permissions are given only to trusted users.

items.title: Campaign templates
items.text: Campaign templates are used in an e-mail campaigns. These template are created and managed on the UI under Campaigns -> Templates, and are selected when creating new campaigns.

items.title: Transactional templates
items.text: Transactional templates are used for sending arbitrary transactional messages using the transactional API. These template are created and managed on the UI under Campaigns -> Templates.

items.title: Template expressions
items.text: There are several template functions and expressions that can be used in campaign and template bodies. They are written in the form {{ .Subscriber.Email }}, that is, an expression between double curly braces {{ and }}.

items.title: Subscriber fields
items.text: Expression Description {{ .Subscriber.UUID }} The randomly generated unique ID of the subscriber {{ .Subscriber.Email }} E-mail ID of the subscriber {{ .Subscriber.Name }} Name of the subscriber {{ .Subscriber.FirstName }} First name of the subscriber (automatically extracted from the name) {{ .Subscriber.LastName }} Last name of the subscriber (automatically extracted from the name) {{ .Subscriber.Status }} Status of the subscriber (enabled, disabled, blocklisted) {{ .Subscriber.Attribs }} Map of arbitrary attributes. Fields can be accessed with ., eg: .Subscriber.Attribs.city {{ .Subscriber.CreatedAt }} Timestamp when the subscriber was first added {{ .Subscriber.UpdatedAt }} Timestamp when the subscriber was modified

items.title: Campaigns
items.text: Expression Description {{ .Campaign.UUID }} The randomly generated unique ID of the campaign {{ .Campaign.Name }} Internal name of the campaign {{ .Campaign.Subject }} E-mail subject of the campaign {{ .Campaign.FromEmail }} The e-mail address from which the campaign is being sent

items.title: Functions
items.text: Function Description {{ Date "2006-01-01" }} Prints the current datetime for the given format expressed as a Go date layout {{ TrackLink "https://link.com" }} Takes a URL and generates a short public tracking URL (/l/...) using PocketBase record ids for the link, campaign, and subscriber (legacy /link/... URLs with UUIDs still work for older messages). https://link.com@TrackLink Shorthand for TrackLink. Eg: <a href="https://link.com@TrackLink">Link</a> {{ TrackView }} Inserts a single tracking pixel. Should only be used once, ideally in the template footer. {{ UnsubscribeURL }} Unsubscription and Manage preferences URL. Ideal for use in the template footer. {{ MessageURL }} URL to view the hosted version of an e-mail message. {{ OptinURL }} URL to the double-optin confirmation page. {{ Safe "<!-- comment -->" }} Add any HTML code as it is.

items.title: Sprig functions
items.text: List Pocket integrates the Sprig library that offers 100+ utility functions for working with strings, numbers, dates etc. that can be used in templating. Refer to the Sprig documentation for the full list of functions.

items.title: Example template
items.text:
The expression {{ template "content" . }} should appear exactly once in every template denoting the spot where an e-mail's content is inserted. Here's a sample HTML e-mail that has a fixed header and footer that inserts the content in the middle.

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
  <head>
    <style>
      body {
        background: #eee;
        font-family: Arial, sans-serif;
        font-size: 6px;
        color: #111;
      }
      header {
        border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;
        padding-bottom: 30px;
        margin-bottom: 30px;
      }
      .container {
        background: #fff;
        width: 450px;
        margin: 0 auto;
        padding: 30px;
      }
    </style>
  </head>
  <body>
    <section class="container">
      <header>
        <!-- This will appear in the header of all e-mails.
             The subscriber's name will be automatically inserted here. //-->
        Hi {{ .Subscriber.FirstName }}!
      </header>

      <!-- This is where the e-mail body will be inserted //-->
      <div class="content">
        {{ template "content" . }}
      </div>

      <footer>
        Copyright 2019. All rights Reserved.
      </footer>

      <!-- The tracking pixel will be inserted here //-->
      {{ TrackView }}
    </section>
  </body>
</html>

Info

For use with plaintext campaigns, create a template with no HTML content and just the placeholder {{ template "content" . }}

items.title: Example campaign body
items.text:
Campaign bodies can be composed using the built-in WYSIWYG editor or as raw HTML documents. Assuming that the subscriber has a set of attributes defined, this example shows how to render those values in a campaign.

Hey, did you notice how the template showed your first name?
Your last name is {{.Subscriber.LastName }}.

You have done {{ .Subscriber.Attribs.projects }} projects.


{{ if eq .Subscriber.Attribs.city "Bengaluru" }}
  You live in Bangalore!
{{ else }}
  Where do you live?
{{ end }}


Here is a link for you to click that will be tracked.
<a href="{{ TrackLink "https://google.com" }}">Google</a>

The above example uses an if condition to show one of two messages depending on the value of a subscriber attribute. Many such dynamic expressions are possible with Go templating expressions.

items.title: System templates
items.text:
System templates are used for rendering public user-facing pages such as the subscription management page, and in automatically generated system e-mails such as the opt-in confirmation e-mail. These are bundled into the binary but can be customized by copying the static directory locally, and passing its path with ./listpocket --static-dir=your/custom/path.

You can fetch the static files with: mkdir -p /home/ubuntu/listpocket/static ; wget -O - https://github.com/compdani/list_pocket/archive/master.tar.gz | tar xz -C /home/ubuntu/listpocket/static --strip=2 "list_pocket-master/static"

Docker example (upstream listmonk), binary service example.

items.title: Public pages
items.text:
/static/public/ index.html Base template with the header and footer that all pages use. home.html Landing page on the root domain with the login button. message.html Generic success / failure message page. optin.html Opt-in confirmation page. subscription.html Subscription management page with options for data export and wipe. subscription-form.html List selection and subscription form page.

To edit the appearance of the public pages using CSS and Javascript, head to Settings > Appearance > Public:

items.title: System e-mails
items.text:
/static/email-templates/ base.html Base template with the header and footer that all system generated e-mails use. campaign-status.html E-mail notification that is sent to admins on campaign start, completion etc. import-status.html E-mail notification that is sent to admins on finish of an import job. subscriber-data.html E-mail that is sent to subscribers when they request a full dump of their private data. subscriber-optin.html Automatic opt-in confirmation e-mail that is sent to an unconfirmed subscriber when they are added. subscriber-optin-campaign.html E-mail content that's inserted into a campaign body when starting an opt-in campaign from the lists page. default.tpl Default campaign template that is created in Campaigns → Templates on first install. This is not used after that.

Info

To turn system e-mail templates to plaintext, remove <!doctype html> from base.html and remove all HTML tags from the templates while retaining the Go templating code.

items.title: Before upgrading
items.text: Always back up PocketBase’s data (pb_data/ by default, or the directory you configured) and any uploaded media or custom static paths before upgrading.

items.title: Standard upgrade
items.text:
1. Stop the running listpocket process.
  2. Replace the binary with a newly built version from the desired commit or release tag.
  3. Start the application again. Migrations run on startup.

If you run under systemd or another supervisor, use the usual stop / start cycle around the binary swap.

items.title: CLI flags --install and --upgrade
items.text: These flags are deprecated no-ops kept for compatibility with older listmonk automation. Migrations run on serve/startup (or via listpocket migrate up). Prefer backing up pb_data and restarting with a new binary.

items.title: Coming from upstream listmonk
items.text: Stock listmonk (PostgreSQL + standalone app) and List Pocket (PocketBase-only) differ in storage and auth. Migrating an existing listmonk instance is not a simple binary swap; plan a dedicated migration (export/import, API sync, or manual data move) and consult the project repository for any migration notes.

items.title: WhatsApp
items.text:
List Pocket can send campaigns and transactional messages on WhatsApp, record delivery and replies, and let staff answer from a subscriber's page. Set it up under Settings → WhatsApp.

It runs on one of two providers, and one is active at a time:

Meta Cloud API Whapi.Cloud Official Yes No Campaign content A template approved in WhatsApp Manager Plain text you write in the campaign Replies Within 24 hours of the person's last message Any time WhatsApp Channel posts Not available Available Default send rate 40 per second 1 per second

Use the Cloud API unless you need Channel posts.

items.title: Risks of Whapi
items.text:
Whapi isn't an official WhatsApp API. It links a phone by QR code.

  • Automating a linked number could get it restricted or banned. There's no reliable figure for how likely that is, or for what volume is safe, and the risk is highest for campaigns to individuals. Use a number you can afford to lose.
  • It could stop working if WhatsApp changes.
  • It's a paid third party that handles your messages.

You have to accept these risks in settings before it can be enabled. The default rate of 1 per second is deliberately cautious, not a known safe rate.

items.title: Setting up the Cloud API
items.text:
You need a Meta app with the WhatsApp use case, a WhatsApp Business Account, a phone number, and a system user token with the whatsapp_business_messaging and whatsapp_business_management permissions.

  1. Enter the token, app secret, a verify token you make up, the phone number ID and the business account ID, then save.
  2. Use Test connection.
  3. In your Meta app, set the webhook to the URL shown in settings, with the same verify token.
  4. Subscribe to the messages and user_preferences webhook fields.

Create templates in WhatsApp Manager. Only approved ones appear in List Pocket.

items.title: Setting up Whapi
items.text:
1. Accept the risk notice, enter your Whapi token and save. The app restarts.
  2. Copy the webhook URL shown in settings into your Whapi channel. It contains a secret, so keep it private.
  3. Enable the messages and statuses events, and users to be told when the phone disconnects.

items.title: Consent
items.text:
WhatsApp has its own consent, separate from email and SMS. A person only gets a campaign if they've consented for one of its lists on WhatsApp and have a phone number. Messaging you isn't consent for campaigns.

Consent can come from:

  • A JOIN message: someone sends JOIN <list uuid>. Share it as a https://wa.me/<number>?text=JOIN%20<list%20uuid> link.
  • A subscriber's page: under Other channels.
  • Copying from SMS: under Settings → WhatsApp. It shows counts before changing anything, and never overrides an opt-out. Run it again to include newer subscribers.

Meta requires that your opt-in named your business and said people would receive messages from it. List Pocket can't check your wording, so copying consent asks you to confirm it.

Sending STOP or UNSUBSCRIBE opts someone out, along with anyone sharing that number, until they opt in again. A person stopping marketing messages in WhatsApp itself does the same. If they later resume, consent isn't restored automatically. An SMS STOP also withdraws consent copied from SMS, but a WhatsApp STOP doesn't affect SMS.

items.title: Campaigns
items.text:
Choose WhatsApp as the campaign's channel.

On the Cloud API, pick a template and fill in its values. A value can include {{name}}, {{first_name}}, {{last_name}} or {{attribs.key}}, and needs a fallback for subscribers where that's empty. Header media, body and header text, and URL button values are supported.

On Whapi, write the message in the Content tab.

Phone numbers need a + and country code. Others are skipped, because the API could otherwise reach the wrong person.

Result What happens Number isn't on WhatsApp (131026) The number is retired and a bounce is recorded. It isn't an opt-out, and a message from that number restores it Person stopped marketing messages (131050) They're opted out Meta's per-user limit (131049) Shown as failed. Not retried automatically Rate limits, or account and template problems Counts as a send error, and too many pause the campaign

Bounces on WhatsApp never run the email bounce actions, so they can't unsubscribe or delete anyone.

As with email and SMS, if a campaign finishes with fewer errors than the pause threshold, those recipients aren't retried automatically.

items.title: Transactional messages
items.text:
Send to /api/tx with messenger set to ch:whatsapp. On the Cloud API, name the template in the data:

{
  "subscriber_record_ids": ["<id>"],
  "template_id": 1,
  "messenger": "ch:whatsapp",
  "data": {
    "whatsapp_template": {
      "name": "order_update",
      "language": "en_US",
      "components": [{ "type": "body", "parameters": [{ "value": "{{first_name}}", "fallback": "there" }] }]
    }
  }
}

The subscriber needs WhatsApp consent. On Whapi, the List Pocket template's text is sent.

items.title: Replies
items.text: A subscriber's page shows their WhatsApp conversation and, with the whatsapp:reply permission, a reply box. On the Cloud API you can only reply within 24 hours of their last message. Nobody who opted out can be messaged. Replies appear on the subscriber's timeline. Inbound media shows as its type, and isn't downloaded.

items.title: WhatsApp Channel posts
items.text:
With Whapi active, Campaigns → WhatsApp Channel posts to channels the linked account administers. This needs the whatsapp:post permission. Posts can be text, an image, a video or a link preview, and can be drafted or scheduled. A link preview needs a title, and its text must include the URL.

A post goes to the channel's followers, so it doesn't use lists or consent. A failed post is never retried automatically, because it might have gone out anyway. Check the channel, then retry it by hand. Whapi suggests 1 to 10 posts a day, and the page warns above that.

items.title: Workflows
items.text: Workflows automate work across contacts, messages and campaigns. Build them on the canvas under Workflows, or ask the AI assistant to draft one. Drafts do nothing until published, and every published version is kept.

items.title: Permissions
items.text:
Workflows run without a signed-in user, so they can do things the person who built them can't. Give these permissions carefully:

Permission Allows workflows:get See workflows and their runs, including the data in those runs workflows:manage Create, edit, test, publish and delete workflows workflows:run Start published workflows and stop runs workflows:approve Approve or deny review steps

items.title: AI settings
items.text: AI steps and the assistant use the same settings: LISTPOCKET_AI_API_KEY, LISTPOCKET_AI_BASE_URL and LISTPOCKET_AI_MODEL. LISTPOCKET_AI_FAST_MODEL and LISTPOCKET_AI_RESEARCH_MODEL are optional. Set budgets on a workflow to limit its spend.

items.title: Format
items.text:
A workflow is a JSON graph of nodes. Written for both people and the AI assistant.

{
  "name": "lead_pipeline",                 // lowercase, digits, _
  "description": "…",
  "trigger": { "type": "manual" },         // see Triggers
  "input_schema": { "type": "object", "properties": { "contact": { "type": "string" } }, "required": ["contact"] },
  "default_input": {},
  "ai": { "budget": { "max_usd_per_run": 0.5, "max_usd_per_day": 5 } },   // models default to LISTPOCKET_AI_* settings
  "nodes": [ … ]
}

items.title: Edges
items.text: Edges live on nodes. next is the single successor. Branches route with cases[].to and default. A ForEach runs body (the first node of a per-item chain) once per item, then continues at next. A Loop runs body again and again, one iteration at a time, until until is true, then continues at next. An empty or missing target ends the path — or, inside a body, ends that item or iteration. No cycles: repeat work with ForEach (over a list) or Loop (until a condition holds). Bodies can't contain another ForEach or Loop.

items.title: Templates and expressions
items.text:
Values in input, value, output, message, review title/data may contain {{ expr }}. A string that is exactly {{ expr }} keeps the expression's type (list, number, object); otherwise it interpolates as text. Conditions (cases[].if, items, until, auto_approve, match, trigger filter) are bare expressions. Language: expr-lang (==, !=, &&, ||, not, in, len(x), filter(list, .tier == 'A'), map(list, .name), x ?? y). Undefined fields are nil.

Environment: input (run input), nodes.<id> (a finished node's output), vars.<name> (a variable from a set node), item and index (inside a ForEach body), loop.iteration and loop.last (inside a Loop body and its until; see below), now (RFC 3339), and run.id.

items.title: Node types
items.text:
type fields output start next — exactly one per workflow the run input agent agent: {system_prompt, tools[], output_schema?, max_steps?, ai?}, input, next {result: <submitted object>, _citations: [...]} — read fields as nodes.<id>.result.<field> tool tool (catalog name), input, next the tool's return value, described by its output_schema in the catalog when it has one branch cases: [{if, to}], default {_next, case} foreach items (expr → list), body, concurrency (default 4), next {count, failed, results: [last output per item]} loop body, until (expr), max_iterations (1–100, required), next {iterations, done, last, results: [last output per iteration]} review review: {title, instructions, data, auto_approve?, on_deny: skip\|continue, timeout?}, next {approved, data (possibly edited), decided_by} wait wait: {delay?: "10m", event?: "<event name>", match?, timeout?}, next {waited} / {event} / {timed_out: true} subworkflow workflow (name), input, next, detach the child run's output; with detach: true, {run_id} right away (the child runs on its own). Input keys that render to nil are left out, so the child's default_input applies notify message, next {message} transform value (template), next the rendered value code code (JavaScript), next the value the code returns, as JSON set variables: [{name, type, value, editor?}], next {<name>: value}; also readable as vars.<name> end output (template) sets the run output

Every node also accepts name (label), on_error: "continue" (failure becomes output {error} and the path continues), and retries (0–5).

Code nodes: the code field is the body of a JavaScript function, so use return. input, nodes, vars, item, index, loop, now and run are globals holding copies of the run data, for example return nodes.search.results.filter((r) => r.score > input.min).length;. item, index and loop are undefined outside a body. Code isn't a template, so {{ }} isn't expanded. It can't reach the network or files and can't call tools, and each run gets 10 seconds and at most 1 MB of output. console.log writes to the app log.

Anyone with workflows:manage can write code nodes. The 10-second limit is the only limit on memory, so code that allocates without stopping can use up the server's memory.

Set nodes: variables run in order, so each can read the ones before it, and a later set node replaces an earlier variable of the same name. Read them as vars.<name> in templates, expressions and code. Inside a ForEach or Loop body, a variable lasts for that item or iteration only. Each variable has a type:

type value result string text the text as written; {{ }} isn't expanded number a number, or a {{ expr }} that gives one a number; anything else fails the node boolean true, false, or a {{ expr }} that gives one a boolean; an empty value is false and anything else fails the node template text with {{ expr }} follows the template rules above code a JavaScript function body, as in a code node the value the code returns html HTML with {{ expr }}; editor is visual or code, for the builder text with interpolated values HTML-escaped, except the values of HTML variables

Use a template variable to insert markup that doesn't come from an HTML variable, and only when it can't contain untrusted data such as inbound messages.

Agent nodes: the system prompt is a Go template over {"input": …} — use {{ .input.market }} (with a dot) there, not expr. Give agents only the tools they need. web.search is provider-side search; web.fetch reads a page. When an agent's result feeds later nodes, set output_schema so the shape is guaranteed. Model roles: "ai": {"model": "@fast"} uses LISTPOCKET_AI_FAST_MODEL (and @research uses LISTPOCKET_AI_RESEARCH_MODEL); both fall back to LISTPOCKET_AI_MODEL.

Loop nodes: inside the body, loop.iteration is the 0-based iteration number (also index) and loop.last is the previous iteration's output (nil on the first — read it as loop.last?.field). After each iteration until is evaluated with loop.last set to that iteration's output (the last body node's output) and nodes.<id> holding that iteration's body outputs — e.g. poll a status: {"id":"poll","type":"loop","body":"check","until":"loop.last.status == 'done'","max_iterations":20,"next":"report"} with a wait node in the body to space the checks out. If until is still false after max_iterations, the loop fails; with on_error: "continue" it outputs done: false and the path continues. Reviews, approvals and waits inside the body pause the run like anywhere else.

A review denied with on_deny: skip (default) ends that path or item. A Tool node whose tool requires_approval pauses for a human before running.

items.title: Triggers
items.text:
• {"type": "manual"} — started from the UI with input.
  • {"type": "cron", "spec": "0 6 * * 1-5", "timezone": "America/Chicago", "overlap": "skip", "input": {…}}
  • {"type": "event", "event": "inbound.email", "filter": "event.contact_id != ''", "input_map": {"contact": "{{ event.contact_id }}"}}
  • {"type": "event", "collection": "subscribers", "on": ["create"], "filter": "record.status == 'enabled'"}
  • {"type": "webhook", "filter": "event.kind == 'signup'", "input_map": {"email": "{{ event.email }}"}} — started by a POST to the workflow's secret URL, with the JSON body as event.

Any workflow can also be run manually. Events are listed by the workflow catalog, and a wait node can pause for one, for example to wait for a reply: {"event": "inbound.email", "match": "event.contact_id == input.contact", "timeout": "72h"}.

items.title: Boards
items.text:
The Move on board and Remove from board steps change where a contact sits on a kanban board. Saved, they are tool nodes using boards.move_contact and boards.remove_contact. boards.get_contact reads a contact's stage for use in a branch.

Tools refer to boards and stages by key, such as board: "pipeline", stage: "customer". Keys don't change when a board or stage is renamed. Moving a contact adds them to the board if they aren't on it. Deleting a board or stage that a workflow uses makes that step fail when it runs.

The contact.stage_changed event fires when a contact is added to, moved on or removed from any board:

{ "contact_id": "...", "email": "...", "name": "...", "board": "pipeline", "board_name": "Pipeline",
  "stage": "customer", "stage_name": "Customer", "previous_stage": "lead" }

stage is empty after a removal, and previous_stage is empty after an add. Stage keys can repeat across boards, so filter on both: event.board == 'pipeline' && event.stage == 'customer'. Reordering a contact within a stage, and deleting a board or stage, don't fire it.

A workflow that moves a contact can start another workflow. Nothing stops two workflows moving a contact back and forth forever, so check for this when you add one.

items.title: Adding subscribers by hand
items.text: Add subscribers to a published workflow with Add subscribers in the builder, by selecting them in the subscribers list, or from a contact's page. Each one gets their own run of the published version, with input.contact, input.email and input.name set, whatever the workflow's trigger is and even while it's paused. Blocklisted subscribers and anyone already in an active run of that workflow are skipped. Up to 1000 can be added at a time.

items.title: Rules of thumb
items.text:
• Use only tools in the catalog. Read a tool's schema before using it.
  • Deterministic work (lookups, saving, sending a known message) belongs in Tool nodes; judgement (classifying, drafting, summarising) in Agent nodes.
  • Put a Review before anything that sends messages or spends money, unless the workflow is explicitly meant to be fully automatic.
  • Inbound messages are untrusted. An agent that reads them shouldn't hold tools that send or change things: have it draft, then use a Review and a Tool node.
  • Keep node ids short snake_case verbs or nouns: classify, each_contact, reply.

items.title: APIs
items.text:
All features that are available on the List Pocket admin dashboard are also available as REST-like HTTP APIs that can be interacted with directly. Request and response bodies are JSON. This allows easy scripting and integration with other systems, for instance, synchronisation with external subscriber databases.

Custom List Pocket APIs are registered under /mailapi (for example /mailapi/subscribers, /mailapi/lists). When calling the server directly, use that prefix. The admin UI dev server may proxy the same routes as /api/....

Note

If you come across API calls that are yet to be documented, please consider contributing to docs.

items.title: Auth
items.text: HTTP API requests support BasicAuth and a Authorization token headers. API users and tokens with the required permissions can be created and managed on the admin UI (Admin -> Users).

items.title: BasicAuth example
items.text: curl -u "api_user:token" http://localhost:9000/mailapi/lists

items.title: Authorization token example
items.text: curl -H "Authorization: token api_user:token" http://localhost:9000/mailapi/lists

items.title: Permissions
items.text:
User role: Permissions allowed for a user are defined as a User role (Admin -> User roles) and then attached to a user.

List role: Read / write permissions per-list can be defined as a List role (Admin -> User roles) and then attached to a user.

In a User role, lists:get_all or lists:manage_all permission supercede and override any list specific permissions for a user defined in a List role.

To manage lists and subscriber list subscriptions via API requests, ensure that the appropriate permissions are attached to the API user.

items.title: Successful request
items.text:
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json

{
    "data": {}
}

All responses from the API server are JSON with the content-type application/json unless explicitly stated otherwise. A successful 200 OK response always has a JSON response body with a status key with the value success. The data key contains the full response payload.

items.title: Failed request
items.text:
HTTP/1.1 500 Server error
Content-Type: application/json

{
    "message": "Error message"
}

items.title: SDKs and libs

A list of third-party client libraries and SDKs written for listmonk APIs. List Pocket aims to keep HTTP APIs compatible with upstream listmonk where possible; these clients may work unchanged or with minor adjustments.

Note

These projects are maintained by their authors against upstream listmonk. Test against your List Pocket instance before relying on them in production.

items.title: API / Subscribers
items.text:
Subscriber identifiers in URLs and JSON are PocketBase record ids (the subscribers.id string returned as id on subscriber objects), not numeric SQLite rowids. Bulk actions use the repeated query parameter subscriber_record_id or the JSON field subscriber_record_ids.

Custom List Pocket APIs are served under /mailapi (for example /mailapi/subscribers). The admin UI dev proxy may expose the same routes as /api/...; use /mailapi when calling the backend directly.

Method Endpoint Description GET /api/subscribers Query and retrieve subscribers. GET /api/subscribers/{id} Retrieve a specific subscriber. GET /api/subscribers/{id}/export Export a specific subscriber. GET /api/subscribers/{id}/bounces Retrieve a subscriber bounce records. GET /api/inbound-email-replies/{replyId}/attachments List inbound email attachments for a timeline email reply event. GET /api/inbound-email-attachments/{id}/download Download an inbound email attachment file. POST /api/subscribers Create a new subscriber. POST /mailapi/subscribers/bulk-add Bulk upsert subscribers from JSON contacts. POST /api/subscribers/{id}/optin Sends optin confirmation email to subscribers. POST /api/public/subscription Create a public subscription. PUT /api/subscribers/lists Modify subscriber list memberships. PUT /mailapi/subscribers/bulk-update Bulk tag/list updates for existing contacts. PUT /api/subscribers/{id} Update a specific subscriber. PUT /api/subscribers/{id}/blocklist Blocklist a specific subscriber. PUT /api/subscribers/blocklist Blocklist one or many subscribers. PUT /api/subscribers/query/blocklist Blocklist subscribers based on SQL expression. DELETE /api/subscribers/{id} Delete a specific subscriber. DELETE /api/subscribers/{id}/bounces Delete a specific subscriber's bounce records. DELETE /api/subscribers Delete one or more subscribers. POST /api/subscribers/query/delete Delete subscribers based on SQL expression.

items.title: GET /api/subscribers
items.text: Retrieve all subscribers.

items.title: Query parameters
items.text: Name Type Required Description search string Free-text match on name, email, or phone (case-insensitive). filters string JSON filter tree for tags, attributes, status, fields, and lists. Does not require subscribers:sql_query. See querying and segmentation. query string Partial SQL expression (requires subscribers:sql_query). list_record_id string PocketBase list record id to filter by. Repeat the query key for multiple lists. subscription_status string Subscription status to filter by if there are one or more list_ids. order_by string Result sorting field. Options: name, status, created_at, updated_at, id (PocketBase record id). order string Sorting order: ASC for ascending, DESC for descending. page number Page number for paginated results. per_page number Results per page. Set as 'all' for all results.

items.title: Example Request
items.text:
curl -u 'api_username:access_token' 'http://localhost:9000/api/subscribers?page=1&per_page=100' 

curl -u 'api_username:access_token' 'http://localhost:9000/api/subscribers?list_record_id=pbc_list_default_001&list_record_id=pbc_list_second_002&page=1&per_page=100'

curl -u 'api_username:access_token' -X GET 'http://localhost:9000/api/subscribers' \
    --url-query 'page=1' \
    --url-query 'per_page=100' \
    --url-query 'filters={"logic":"and","rules":[{"field":"attrib","key":"city","op":"eq","value":"Bengaluru"}]}'

curl -u 'api_username:access_token' -X GET 'http://localhost:9000/api/subscribers' \
    --url-query 'page=1' \
    --url-query 'per_page=100' \
    --url-query "query=subscribers.name LIKE 'Test%' AND json_extract(subscribers.attribs, '$.city') = 'Bengaluru'"

items.title: PUT /mailapi/subscribers/bulk-update
items.text:

Default: unconfirmed.

At least one of tags_add, tags_remove, list_remove, or list_update must be provided.

items.title: POST /mailapi/subscribers/bulk-add
items.text:
Bulk upsert subscribers from JSON contact objects. Behavior is similar to CSV import, but runs synchronously and accepts structured JSON instead of a file upload. Creates new subscribers or updates existing ones matched by email.

Requires permission: subscribers:import.

Maximum batch size: 5,000 contacts per request.

List record ids in list_remove and list_update are filtered against the authenticated user's list manage permissions. Updating an existing subscriber requires access to at least one of that subscriber's lists (same as other subscriber manage APIs).

items.title: Parameters
items.text: Name Type Required Description contacts object[] Yes Contact objects (see table below). tags_add string[] Tags merged into each contact after upsert. tags_remove string[] Tags removed from each contact after upsert. list_remove string[] PocketBase list record ids to remove each contact from. list_update string[] PocketBase list record ids to add or update membership on. subscription_status string Status for list_update. Default: unconfirmed. override_details bool When true, overwrite profile fields on email conflict. Default: false.

items.title: Contact object fields
items.text:
Each item in contacts supports the following fields:

Name Type Required Description email string Yes Subscriber email address. phone string Phone number. name string Full name. Derived from email local-part if omitted on create. first_name string First name. last_name string Last name. attribs JSON Custom attributes stored on the subscriber. attributes JSON Alias for attribs (same as CSV import column name).

When override_details is false and the email already exists, existing phone, name fields, and attribs are preserved. When true, incoming contact fields replace those values on conflict.

Global tags_add, tags_remove, list_update, and list_remove are applied to every contact in the batch after each upsert.

items.title: Response fields
items.text: Name Type Description ok bool Always true on success. matched number Contacts successfully upserted (created + updated). skipped number Invalid or empty contact entries skipped during processing. created number New subscribers inserted. updated number Existing subscribers matched by email. tags_updated number Contacts whose tags were updated. lists_removed number List membership rows removed. lists_updated number List membership rows inserted or updated.

items.title: Example Request
items.text:
curl -u 'api_username:access_token' -X POST 'http://localhost:9000/mailapi/subscribers/bulk-add' \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--data-raw '{"contacts":[{"email":"john@example.com","first_name":"John","last_name":"Doe","attribs":{"city":"Berlin"}}],"tags_add":["vip"],"list_update":["pbc_list_a_004"],"subscription_status":"confirmed","override_details":false}'

    "matched": 1,
    "skipped": 0,
    "created": 1,
    "updated": 0,

items.title: API / Transactional
items.text: Method Endpoint Description POST /api/tx Send transactional messages

items.title: POST /api/tx
items.text: Allows sending transactional messages to one or more subscribers via a preconfigured transactional template.

items.title: Parameters
items.text: Name Type Required Description subscriber_email string Email of the subscriber. Can substitute with subscriber_record_ids / deprecated subscriber_id. subscriber_id number Deprecated integer rowid. Prefer subscriber_record_ids. subscriber_emails string[] Multiple subscriber emails as alternative to subscriber_email. subscriber_ids number[] Deprecated integer rowids. Prefer subscriber_record_ids. subscriber_record_ids string[] PocketBase subscriber record IDs (preferred over subscriber_ids). subscriber_mode string Subscriber lookup mode: default, fallback, or external template_id number Yes ID of the transactional template to be used for the message. from_email string Optional sender email. subject string Optional subject. If empty, the subject defined on the template is used data JSON Optional nested JSON map. Available in the template as {{ .Tx.Data.* }}. headers JSON[] Optional array of email headers. messenger string Messenger to send the message. Default is email. content_type string Email format options include html, markdown, and plain. preheader string Optional inbox preview text auto-injected for HTML messages.

items.title: Subscriber modes
items.text:
The subscriber_mode parameter controls how the recipients (subscribers or non-subscriber recipients) are resolved.

Mode Description default Recipients must exist as subscribers in the database. Pass either subscriber_emails or subscriber_record_ids (or deprecated subscriber_ids). fallback Only accepts subscriber_emails and looks up subscribers in the database. If not found, sends the message to the e-mail anyway. In the template, apart from {{ .Subscriber.Email }}, other subscriber fields such as .Name. will be empty. Use {{ Tx.Data.* }} instead. external Sends to the given subscriber_emails without subscriber lookup in the database. In the template, apart from {{ .Subscriber.Email }}, other subscriber fields such as .Name. will be empty. Use {{ Tx.Data.* }} instead.

items.title: Example
items.text:
curl -u "api_user:token" "http://localhost:9000/api/tx" -X POST \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8' \
     --data-binary @- << EOF
    {
        "subscriber_email": "user@test.com",
        "template_id": 2,
        "data": {"order_id": "1234", "date": "2022-07-30", "items": [1, 2, 3]},
        "content_type": "html"
    }
EOF

items.title: Example response
items.text:
{
    "data": true
}

items.title: Example with external mode
items.text:
Send to arbitrary email addresses without requiring them to be subscribers:

curl -u "api_user:token" "http://localhost:9000/api/tx" -X POST \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8' \
     --data-binary @- << EOF
    {
        "subscriber_mode": "external",
        "subscriber_emails": ["recipient@example.com"],
        "template_id": 2,
        "data": {"name": "John", "order_id": "1234"},
        "content_type": "html"
    }
EOF

In the template, use {{ .Tx.Data.name }}, {{ .Tx.Data.order_id }}, etc. to access the data.

items.title: File Attachments
items.text:
To include file attachments in a transactional message, use the multipart/form-data Content-Type. Use data param for the parameters described above as a JSON object. Include any number of attachments via the file param.

curl -u "api_user:token" "http://localhost:9000/api/tx" -X POST \
-F 'data=\"{
    \"subscriber_email\": \"user@test.com\",
    \"template_id\": 4
}"' \
-F 'file=@"/path/to/attachment.pdf"' \
-F 'file=@"/path/to/attachment2.pdf"'

items.title: Performance
items.text:
List Pocket is built to be highly performant and can handle millions of subscribers with minimal system resources.

As the SQLite database (managed by embedded PocketBase) grows—with a large number of subscribers, campaign views, and click records—counting records and aggregating statistics can slow down. For instance, loading admin pages that do these aggregations can take tens of seconds if the database has millions of subscribers.

  • Aggregate counts and statistics on the landing dashboard.
  • Subscriber count beside every list on the Lists page.

On installations with millions of subscribers, where those pages do not load instantly, turn on Settings → Performance → Cache slow database queries.

items.title: Slow query caching
items.text:
When this option is enabled, dashboard counts and list subscriber counts are no longer computed on every request. Instead they are stored in the listpocket_stats_cache collection and refreshed on a crontab (default: 0 3 * * *, 3 AM daily). Use crontab.guru to generate an expression.

Dashboard charts stay live (they are timezone-dependent) and are aggregated in SQL.

Bulk subscriber import also refreshes the cache when it finishes.

items.title: Maintenance (SQLite)
items.text: Scheduled maintenance runs PRAGMA optimize, ANALYZE, and PRAGMA incremental_vacuum, then a full VACUUM to reclaim space. Schedule this during low-traffic windows: VACUUM takes an exclusive lock while it runs. incremental_vacuum only reclaims pages when the database was created with PRAGMA auto_vacuum=INCREMENTAL.
